title: The Portrait of Little Hawley
premise: Zephyrine Okafor, the cathedral's meticulous archivist, has spent a decade making herself unremarkable—until a drowned stranger is found in the locked crypt wearing clothes cut from her own wardrobe, down to her mother's brooch. The dead man is identified as Little Hawley, a child declared dead thirty years ago in the same crypt, the case that made the cathedral's founding families untouchable. As the anniversary dinner of the 'closed' tragedy approaches, Zephyrine discovers the victim was blackmailing five prominent families with proof that the original death was a murder they covered up—and that her own late mother, the cathedral's forgotten seamstress, stitched the evidence into an altar cloth. In the climax, at the anniversary dinner itself, Zephyrine unveils the cloth and forces a confession from the last surviving conspirator, choosing visibility over survival; the epilogue closes with her adopting the name she was born with and the crypt finally opened to daylight.
about_author: Yara Thornbury is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing births, deaths, and the silences between them in northern England. They write mysteries about people history tried to file away.

chapters.title: The Locked Door Below
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Establishes her ordered life among the cathedral archives and her ritual of avoiding attention. The sexton reports the crypt seal broken for the first time in thirty years. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine descends with police and recognizes the drowned man's clothing as hers—the grey coat, her mother's brooch pinned at the throat. Detective Inspector Ferro notes her reaction. Emotional beat: violation, the collapse of invisibility.

chapters.title: Little Hawley
chapters.summary: The victim's fingerprints match a boy who died in 1994, whose funeral Zephyrine's mother sewed the shroud for. The town insists the case is closed. POV shifts briefly to Ferro. Emotional beat: uncanny return of the past.

chapters.title: Five Names on a List
chapters.summary: Searching the victim's rented room, Zephyrine finds a ledger of payments signed by five initials belonging to the cathedral's founding families. She hides it from Ferro. Emotional beat: complicity begins; she chooses secrecy.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Invitations arrive for the thirtieth-anniversary memorial dinner honoring the Hawley tragedy. Zephyrine, as archivist, must attend. A threatening note appears in her archive drawer. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, memory chapter: her mother's late-night sewing, the altar cloth commissioned by the families, her mother's sudden death weeks after the original funeral. Emotional beat: grief reframed as suspicion.

chapters.title: The Seamstress's Stitch
chapters.summary: Examining the altar cloth under raking light, Zephyrine finds letters worked into the hem—a confession fragment naming one conspirator. Someone else has been searching the vestry. Emotional beat: discovery and fear.

chapters.title: Lady Verity's Tea
chapters.summary: Zephyrine accepts tea with matriarch Verity Ashcombe, who probes gently about the crypt and offers money for silence. POV alternates with Verity's, revealing genuine love tangled with guilt. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Ferro's autopsy findings show the victim survived a drowning as a child—scarred lungs prove Little Hawley didn't die in 1994; he lived. The question becomes: who did die? Emotional beat: the case cracks open.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Zephyrine opens the 1994 burial register and finds the coffin weighed forty pounds less than it should. The buried child was someone else entirely. Emotional beat: horror at the substitution.

chapters.title: An Archivist's Enemies
chapters.summary: Her flat is searched; the ledger is gone but a copy she hid in a hymnal survives. Ferro reveals he knows she withheld evidence and gives her one chance. Emotional beat: cornered, alliance offered.

chapters.title: Verity's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Verity, dying, admits the five families covered up an accidental death during a christening gone wrong—but swears the buried child's identity is a secret even she fears. Emotional beat: pity entwined with manipulation.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Following her mother's stitch-code, Zephyrine locates an unmarked grave behind the almshouse: a small coffin, exhumed long ago, refilled with stones. Emotional beat: desecration of the innocent.

chapters.title: Brother Anselm's Silence
chapters.summary: The elderly monk who sealed the crypt in 1994 finally speaks: he saw a woman carry a living child out that night—and he has been paid to forget ever since. Emotional beat: the cost of bought silence.

chapters.title: One of Five Falls
chapters.summary: Conspirator number two, Aldous Pike, is found dead in his boathouse hours before he was to meet Zephyrine. The killer is inside the circle—or beside her. Emotional beat: escalating danger, isolation.

chapters.title: The Name Under the Brooch
chapters.summary: Zephyrine discovers the brooch's locket holds a lock of hair and a hospital tag: the buried child was her own infant brother, swapped for the stillborn heir of another family. Emotional beat: devastating personal revelation.

chapters.title: Why She Sewed
chapters.summary: Reassembling the cloth's full cipher, Zephyrine learns her mother witnessed the swap and hid the truth where only her daughter would look—then died for it. Emotional beat: inheritance of truth as burden and gift.

chapters.title: The Last Conspirator
chapters.summary: Ferro and Zephyrine identify the killer: the surviving heir, now the dinner's host, who killed Hawley to stop the blackmail before it unraveled his stolen identity. Emotional beat: cold clarity before the storm.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: At the dinner, Zephyrine stands before the town, unfurls the altar cloth, and reads the cipher aloud as the killer moves toward her. Ferro intervenes; the arrest happens under the chandeliers. Emotional beat: climax—visibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: Opening the Crypt
chapters.summary: The crypt is unsealed for the first time in thirty years; the false coffin is opened publicly and the stone-filled lie exposed. The town's founding myth collapses. Emotional beat: collective reckoning.

chapters.title: A Grave With Her Name On It
chapters.summary: Zephyrine buries her brother properly beside her mother, using the shroud pattern her mother designed. Verity leaves her the Ashcombe papers, trusting her to archive the truth honestly. Emotional beat: mourning turned to peace.

chapters.title: The Portrait of Little Hawley
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Zephyrine's POV. She hangs a commissioned portrait of her brother in the archive, signs the accession book with her full birth name, and leaves the crypt door unlocked. Emotional beat: found family, inherited truth, home.
